alabama.designatedAgent: Yes. Notarized affidavit designating an agent; statutory form provided in the section. (Ala. Code § 34-13-11(a)(2))
alabama.cremationAuthorizer: The 'authorizing agent' under Ala. Code § 34-13-11; written cremation authorization required by § 34-13-121.
alabama.majorityRule: Majority required for the children, grandchildren, sibling, and grandparent classes; less than a majority may act after reasonable notification efforts if not aware of opposition by more than half. Any one person of the same degree may act in the next-of-kin class.
alabama.holdRemains: No specific statute found. No Alabama statute was found that expressly allows or prohibits a funeral home from withholding remains over an unpaid bill, so the signed contract and general consumer-protection law govern.

alaska.designatedAgent: Yes. Disposition document (statutory form at AS 13.75.030); the agent must sign the document for the appointment to be effective. (AS 13.75.010, 13.75.030, 13.75.040)
alaska.cremationAuthorizer: The person authorized to control disposition under AS 13.75.020; cremation may not be performed contrary to a disposition document (AS 13.75.070)
alaska.majorityRule: Majority required for adult children and for kindred classes with more than two members; fewer than half of the adult children may act after reasonable notification efforts if not aware of opposition by one-half or more.
alaska.holdRemains: No specific statute found. No Alaska statute was found that expressly allows or prohibits a funeral home from withholding remains over an unpaid bill, so the signed contract and general consumer-protection law govern.

arizona.designatedAgent: Yes. The decedent's own written statement directing cremation/disposition (signed, dated, and notarized or witnessed) controls without anyone's concurrence; agent designation runs through a health care or durable power of attorney, but that agent ranks behind the spouse under § 36-831. (A.R.S. § 32-1365.01; § 36-831(A)(2))
arizona.cremationAuthorizer: The authorizing agent in the § 36-831 order must give written consent (A.R.S. § 32-1365.02); the decedent's own written statement can self-authorize cremation (§ 32-1365.01)
arizona.majorityRule: Any one member of a class may act unless an objection is known; if there is an objection, the majority of the reasonably available members of the class decides (§ 36-831(D)).
arizona.holdRemains: No specific statute found. No Arizona statute was found that expressly allows or prohibits a funeral home from withholding remains over an unpaid bill, so the signed contract and general consumer-protection law govern.

district-of-columbia.holdRemains: No specific statute found. No District of Columbia statute was found that expressly allows or prohibits a funeral home from withholding remains over an unpaid bill, so the signed contract and general consumer-protection law govern.

mississippi.holdRemains: No specific statute found. No Mississippi statute was found that expressly allows or prohibits a funeral home from withholding remains over an unpaid bill, so the signed contract and general consumer-protection law govern.

new-jersey.holdRemains: No specific statute found. No New Jersey statute was found that expressly allows or prohibits a funeral home from withholding remains over an unpaid bill, so the signed contract and general consumer-protection law govern.

Funeral-industry practice calls the written version a 'Statement of Contrary Intent.' Health & Safety Code §§ 716.051, 716.052. Waiting period: a crematory may not cremate within 48 hours of the time of death on the death certificate unless waived in writing by a justice of the peace or medical examiner of the county of death, or by court order, § 716.004(a)
texas.majorityRule: Any one - no majority required; the statute grants the right to 'any one of' the adult children, 'either one of' the parents, and 'any one of' the adult siblings
texas.holdRemains: Prohibited - refusing to promptly surrender a dead human body to a person or agent authorized to make funeral arrangements is a violation, Tex. Occupations Code § 651.456(2). No specific statute found allowing a lien/withholding for an unpaid bill.

priorityOrder: Person designated in a written instrument (notarized or executed with will formalities), or person designated by a service member on DD Form 93
Surviving, legally recognized spouse (unless a personal representative was nominated by the decedent after the marriage, in which case that nominee takes priority over the spouse)
Person nominated as personal representative in a will executed with the formalities of § 75-2-502
Sole surviving child, or majority of surviving children
Surviving parent or parents
Surviving sibling, or majority of surviving siblings
Next degree of kinship in descending order under descent and distribution (any person of that degree if more than one)
Guardian at time of death, if any
Any public official charged with arranging disposition of deceased persons
Any other willing person, including the personal representative or the funeral service director with custody, after written attestation of a good-faith effort to contact those listed above
utah.designatedAgent: Yes. Written instrument acknowledged before a notary public or executed with the same formalities required of a will under § 75-2-502 (a power of attorney that terminates at death is expressly excluded); a person may also give advance directions for their own disposition under § 58-9-601. (Utah Code §§ 58-9-602(1), 58-9-601)
utah.cremationAuthorizer: Authorizing agent - the person holding the right of disposition under Utah Code § 58-9-602, which expressly may include cremation, signing a cremation authorization form (see § 58-9-606, right to rely on a signed cremation authorization form)
utah.majorityRule: Majority required for children and siblings; less than one-half / less than a majority is vested if they used reasonable efforts to notify all others in the class and are not aware of opposition from more than one-half of the class
utah.holdRemains: No specific statute found. No Utah statute was found that expressly allows or prohibits a funeral home from withholding remains over an unpaid bill, so the signed contract and general consumer-protection law govern.

priorityOrder: Decedent's own written directive (controls before the list below applies)
Individual appointed to arrange disposition under an advance directive (18 V.S.A. ch. 231)
Surviving spouse
Sole surviving child, or majority of surviving children
Custodial / primary-care parent (for a minor or disabled decedent), or sole surviving parent / both parents
Sole surviving sibling, or majority of surviving siblings
Any other family member, in descending order of kinship (majority of same degree)
Guardian of the decedent at time of death
Any other willing individual, incl. estate representative (after written attestation of good-faith effort to contact those above)
Funeral director / disposition facility operator with custody of the body (after written attestation)
Office of the Chief Medical Examiner (when it has jurisdiction and custody, after written attestation)
vermont.designatedAgent: Yes. Advance Directive (18 V.S.A. ch. 231) - adult may direct disposition of remains and appoint an individual to arrange disposition and funeral goods/services. (18 V.S.A. § 9702(a)(16) and (a)(18); appointee is #1 in § 5227(a)(1))
vermont.cremationAuthorizer: The person holding the right of disposition under 18 V.S.A. § 5227 (highest-priority available person in the order above)
vermont.majorityRule: Majority required for surviving children, siblings, and same-degree family members; less than a majority may act if they made prompt, reasonable efforts to contact/notify all others and know of no opposition - 18 V.S.A. § 5227(b)
vermont.holdRemains: Silent - No specific statute found prohibiting or allowing withholding for an unpaid bill (18 V.S.A. § 5231 separately lets a funeral director refuse/retain remains while a court disposition dispute is pending, not for debt)

priorityOrder: Person designated under Va. Code section 54.1-2825 (expressly has priority over all others)

All other next of kin as defined in section 54.1-2800 (spouse, adult children, parents, siblings, guardians, grandparents, and other relatives). Virginia law lists them 'regardless of the relationship to the decedent' and does not rank them against each other
virginia.designatedAgent: Yes. Signed and notarized written designation, accepted in writing by the designee; a copy must reach the funeral establishment (and cemetery, if any) no later than 48 hours after the establishment receives the remains. DD Form 93 designee controls for qualifying military deaths. (Va. Code § 54.1-2825)
virginia.cremationAuthorizer: Next of kin or his representative - which includes the § 54.1-2825 designee, an agent named in an advance directive (§ 54.1-2984), or a guardian - who signs the cremation authorization form and provides visual identification (Va. Code § 54.1-2818.1; 18VAC65-20-436)
virginia.majorityRule: None. The statute sets no majority rule and no priority among next of kin; if next of kin disagree, any of them may petition the circuit court to decide (Va. Code section 54.1-2807.01). Since 2025, a funeral home notified of a dispute may proceed after 30 days with no agreement or court order.
virginia.holdRemains: Silent - No specific statute found prohibiting or allowing withholding for an unpaid bill (Va. Code § 54.1-2808.1 only permits a funeral director to dispose of cremains unclaimed after 120 days)
virginia.statuteCite: Va. Code § 54.1-2825 (with 'next of kin' defined in § 54.1-2800)
virginia.note: Virginia is the outlier state: Va. Code section 54.1-2800 defines next of kin 'regardless of the relationship to the decedent' and does not rank kin against each other. Only a section 54.1-2825 designee has express priority; if kin disagree, any of them may petition the circuit court to decide (section 54.1-2807.01).

priorityOrder: Decedent's own witnessed written wishes / prepaid or filed prearrangement (controls first, RCW 68.50.160(1)-(2))
Person designated on decedent's DD Form 93 (if decedent died in qualifying military service)
Designated agent (written document signed and dated by decedent in presence of a witness)
Surviving spouse or state registered domestic partner
Majority of surviving adult children
Surviving parents
Majority of surviving siblings
Court-appointed guardian at time of death
washington.designatedAgent: Yes. Written document signed and dated by the decedent in the presence of a witness designating an agent to direct disposition; prepaid/filed prearrangements under ch. 68.46 RCW / RCW 18.39.280-18.39.345 also cannot be cancelled or substantially revised by survivors. (RCW 68.50.160(3)(b))
washington.cremationAuthorizer: The person(s) determined under RCW 68.50.160 as having authority to order cremation/disposition; that person is also entitled to possession of the cremated remains under RCW 68.50.270.
washington.majorityRule: Majority expressly required - statute vests the right in 'the majority of the surviving adult children' and 'the majority of the surviving siblings' - RCW 68.50.160(3)(d), (f)
washington.holdRemains: Prohibited - detaining or claiming to detain any human remains for any debt or demand, or on any pretended lien or charge, is a gross misdemeanor - RCW 68.50.120

priorityOrder: Decedent's preneed funeral contract directions (control any matter they address, W. Va. Code § 30-6-22a(a))
Person designated in a notarized affidavit executed under § 30-6-22a(b)(1)
Surviving spouse
Sole surviving child, or majority of surviving children
Surviving parent or parents
Surviving brother or sister, or majority of surviving siblings
Surviving grandparent, or majority of surviving grandparents
Adult grandchildren
Guardian of the person at time of death
Personal representative of the decedent's estate
Person in next degree of kinship, descending order under laws of descent and distribution (any one person of the same degree may act)
Public officer/administrator responsible, if disposition is a state or political-subdivision responsibility
Any other willing person, incl. funeral director with custody (after written attestation of good-faith effort to contact those above)
west-virginia.designatedAgent: Yes. Affidavit executed before a notary public in substantially the statutory form in § 30-6-22a(b)(1)(B) designating a person with the right to control disposition; a preneed funeral contract (W. Va. Code § 47-14-2) may also direct disposition. (W. Va. Code § 30-6-22a(b)(1))
west-virginia.cremationAuthorizer: The authorized representative / person holding the right of disposition under § 30-6-22a, who must give written permission on the Board-prescribed form; a separate medical examiner / coroner cremation permit is also required - W. Va. Code § 30-6-21.
west-virginia.majorityRule: Majority required for children, siblings, and grandparents; less than a majority (children: less than one-half) may act if they used reasonable efforts to notify all others and are not aware of opposition by more than one-half - § 30-6-22a(b)(3), (5), (6). For the next-degree-of-kinship class, any one person of that degree may act.
west-virginia.holdRemains: Silent - No specific statute found prohibiting or allowing withholding for an unpaid bill

priorityOrder: Representative (or successor representative) named in decedent's Authorization for Final Disposition
Surviving spouse
Surviving child, or majority of surviving children
Surviving parent or parents
Surviving sibling, or majority of surviving siblings
Individual in class of next degree of kinship, descending order (Wis. Stat. § 990.001(16))
Guardian of the person of the decedent
Any other willing individual (after written attestation of good-faith effort to contact those above)
wisconsin.designatedAgent: Yes. Authorization for Final Disposition - voluntary written document executed by an adult of sound mind under Wis. Stat. § 154.30(8), naming a representative and successor representative(s); a federal DoD form designating a person to direct disposition for a service member is also recognized (§ 154.30(8)(dm)) (Wis. Stat. § 154.30(2)(a)1. and (8))
wisconsin.cremationAuthorizer: An 'authorizing agent' under Wis. Stat. § 440.72 - in order: surviving spouse; one surviving adult child who confirms in writing that all other surviving children were notified; a surviving parent; the surviving individual in the closest degree of kinship; any other person (each lower tier only if higher tiers decline, are dead/incapacitated, and do not object). The § 154.30 priority holder controls final disposition generally.
wisconsin.majorityRule: Majority required for surviving children and for surviving siblings, except a minority may act if it used reasonable efforts to notify all others and is not aware of opposition by the majority - Wis. Stat. § 154.30(2)(a)3., 5.; probate court designates who controls if same-level individuals cannot agree (§ 154.30(3)(c))
wisconsin.holdRemains: Silent - No specific statute found prohibiting or allowing withholding for an unpaid bill (Wis. Stat. § 154.30(5)(b) allows a provider to retain, embalm or refrigerate remains while a priority dispute awaits agreement/court decision and add that cost, but that is dispute retention, not a debt lien)
wisconsin.note: Wisconsin has two overlapping lists: section 154.30 for disposition generally and section 440.72 for who may sign a cremation authorization, and they are not identical (one adult child can authorize cremation where disposition generally may require more). A would-be controller can also lose the right by failing to exercise it within 2 days of notification.

priorityOrder: Decedent's written instructions, or person designated in decedent's document to direct disposition (controls first, Wyo. Stat. § 2-17-101(a))
Decedent's spouse at time of death
Adult child of the decedent
Either parent of the decedent
Adult sibling of the decedent
Grandparent of the decedent
Stepchild of the decedent
Guardian of the decedent (per Wyo. Stat. § 3-2-201(a)(x))
wyoming.designatedAgent: Yes. A document that designates and authorizes another person to direct disposition of the decedent's body (§ 2-17-101(a)); the optional statutory 'Disposition of Remains' form in Wyo. Stat. § 2-17-102 lets a person state burial/cremation wishes and designate someone to arrange disposition if no prior arrangements were made. A military designation on a federally mandated form is expressly recognized. (Wyo. Stat. §§ 2-17-101(a), 2-17-102)
wyoming.cremationAuthorizer: Signed consent of the designated person under the decedent's document, or otherwise the highest-priority available person in the § 2-17-101(b) order (funeral service practitioner must obtain signed consent before burial/cremation proceeds); if no consent is received within 7 days of death, the county coroner may consent (§ 2-17-101(d))
wyoming.majorityRule: No majority-of-class rule as such - any one person in the priority class may consent, but if contrary written consents arrive from members of the same highest-priority class, the practitioner must follow the directive supported by the greatest number of consents in that class; a higher- or equal-priority contrary consent within 3 days also blocks action - Wyo. Stat. § 2-17-101(c)
wyoming.holdRemains: Silent - No specific statute found prohibiting or allowing withholding for an unpaid bill
